outcomes: Implement exact causal attention over key tiles
Verify tiled output against a full oracle
Map grouped query heads to shared key/value heads

Share keys and values across query heads

online-softmax.name: online softmax
online-softmax.definition: A recurrence for updating a stable softmax maximum and denominator incrementally.
online-softmax.explanation: Online softmax keeps a running maximum and a sum of exponentials shifted by that maximum. When a larger score appears, it rescales the old sum to the new reference before adding the new term. The same state can merge score tiles. Attention also carries a value-weighted numerator on that scale, allowing exact normalized output without storing every individual score value.

tiled-attention.name: tiled attention
tiled-attention.definition: Attention evaluated over bounded query, key, or value blocks.
tiled-attention.explanation: Tiled attention computes small score blocks and combines them while retaining only compact running normalization state. In an exact algorithm every permitted query-key pair is still evaluated, so arithmetic remains quadratic for dense attention. The benefit is avoiding a full quadratic score or probability tensor and improving memory locality. Hardware speed depends on block shapes, fusion, and the memory hierarchy.

grouped-query-attention.name: grouped-query attention
grouped-query-attention.definition: Several query heads sharing each key and value head.
grouped-query-attention.explanation: Grouped-query attention uses Hq query heads but fewer Hkv key/value heads. Equal groups of Hq/Hkv queries read one shared K/V head. It interpolates between ordinary multi-head attention, where counts match, and multi-query attention, where one K/V head serves all queries. This reduces K/V projections and decoder-cache traffic, though dense pairwise attention work still grows quadratically with the complete sequence length.

checks: Tiled attention matches the full oracle within 2e-6 + 2e-6 times absolute reference across tile sizes
First causal output equals its only visible value
Increasing maxima preserve a hand-computed weighted numerator
Invalid or overflowing shapes and nonfinite scores are rejected
GQA requires a divisible head mapping
A maximum-sized tile does not overflow index arithmetic
limitations: Scalar CPU code demonstrates the recurrence, not FlashAttention hardware performance
Full oracle stores one score row rather than an entire quadratic tensor
Random tensors do not measure trained-model quality
No backward pass or block-sparse approximation is implemented
Benchmark measures allocating end-to-end CPU functions, not allocation-free kernels
